A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CheY(N23) and CheZ are two proteins that interact to regulate the tumble signal in chemotaxis and that this interaction is mediated by the N termini of both proteins.
the CheZ protein has a specific binding surface for the CheY protein.
CheY and CheZ have a complex interplay of interactions which are required for the regulation of the flagellar switch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CheY(N23) and CheZ proteins have a direct interaction, which is important for the CheZ dephosphorylating activity.
CheZ and CheY have a complex relationship and that the interaction between the two proteins may involve a dynamic equilibrium between multiple binding modes.
the binding of CheZ to the phosphorylation site of CheY is a critical step in the regulation of the CheY phosphorylation state and the chemotactic response.
